_comment: Shared fixtures for the peq-scores <-> _quality mirror pair.
Read by BOTH plan-dashboard/scripts/lib/peq-scores.test.mjs AND
tests/test_peq_mirror.py. Neither side owns this file.
AUTHORITY. This is a TRIPLE, not a pair. scripts/podcast/_rules.py holds
R_INTEREST_WEIGHT and the five R_INTEREST_* pattern lists; _quality.py IMPORTS
them (WEIGHT_INTEREST = R_INTEREST_WEIGHT); peq-scores.ts RE-TYPES them as
literals with no link to the authority. So the constants below are asserted
against _rules.py on the Python side, not against _quality.py - otherwise
_rules.py could change the weight, _quality.py's sum-to-1.0 assert could still
pass if another weight compensated, and the TypeScript 0.15 would diverge with
nothing complaining.
TWO REAL DIVERGENCES were found here on 2026-07-26 and fixed at the root. Both
were provable in isolation and LATENT in practice - measured across all 58
chapter sources in the repo, zero were affected, so no shipped verdict moved.
1. ROUNDING. Math.round is half-UP; Python's round() is half-to-EVEN. 82.25
-> 82.3 in TS and 82.2 in Python. Enumerating every value from 0 to 100 at
3-decimal granularity: 500 of 100,001 diverge. Fixed by an explicit
roundHalfEven() in peq-scores.ts - NOT by a test tolerance.
HONEST SCOPE, because the obvious claim is wrong: NONE of those 500 can
flip a PASS/WARN/FAIL verdict. A flip would need 84.95 or 69.95, and at
both the nearest double sits ABOVE the tie so half-to-even never engages -
Python and Math.round agree there. The displayed score could disagree with
the gated score by 0.1; the VERDICT could not. Both boundary values are
pinned below precisely because they are the cases people assume diverge.
2. WORD BOUNDARIES. Python's \b is Unicode-aware, JavaScript's is ASCII-only,
so `دobjectionد` matched in TS and not in Python. In an Arabic-source
project, Arabic-adjacent English is precisely the text at risk. Fixed by
spelling the boundary out as a Unicode-aware lookaround on the TS side -
the same construction anchorKey needed for \d in July.
Python is canonical throughout: _quality.score gates real bundles via
assemble_bundle.py and challenger_scoring.py, while peq-scores.ts only displays.
